subject: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

Sean — I need your read on whether we should ship a 1.19.x hotfix this week with the TP stability changes.

Context: after the 2/13 Sev1, Runtime has a focused set of fixes (cancellation/barrier deadlock, async error propagation, TP-group watchdog/quarantine + metrics). We can cut 1.19.1 off rc2 today if we’re aligned.

Asks:
1) From an SRE standpoint, are we comfortable shipping these as a hotfix vs waiting for 1.20?
2) If “go,” what rollout guardrails are mandatory (canary %, soak time, rollback triggers, oncall coverage)?

Attaching the current risk matrix + change summary.

- Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: runtime-1.19.1-hotfix-risk-matrix_v3.xlsx (XLSX)
Attachment: tp-stability_hotfix-change-summary_1.19.1-rc2.pdf (PDF)


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

Mateo — leaning “go” but only with strict rollout controls.

Why I’m okay with a hotfix:
- The Sev1 failure mode is high customer pain + expensive oncall (stuck TP groups that keep getting traffic).
- The mitigations are targeted and give us better failure-domain control (quarantine a TP group vs letting it poison the pool).

Main risks I want called out:
1) Watchdog false positives under legitimate long-step decode (could turn “slow” into “reset”).
2) Any change that touches cancellation/barriers can introduce new deadlocks or throughput regressions.
3) Error propagation changes can surface previously-silent NCCL issues; that’s good, but it can look like “more errors” initially.

Guardrails I’d require:
- Canary in Hosted only first (us-east, then us-west): start 1% of TP traffic, then 5%, then 25% only after 2h soak each.
- Rollback triggers (any one):
  - +0.3% absolute increase in 5xx over baseline for TP routes
  - p99 end-to-end latency regression >10% for the top 3 TP-backed models
  - watchdog_quarantine_rate >0.5% of TP groups/hour sustained for >30m
  - tp_collective_timeout_count non-zero sustained (we can tolerate a few during the first hour if correlated to driver issues, but not a rising trend)
- SRE oncall should be heads-up and we should have a pre-written mitigation: flip feature flag to disable quarantine behavior and/or raise thresholds (I know there are new knobs in pr-18473).

If you can commit to: perf-canary pass + 24h canary before broad enablement, I’m comfortable.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:34 AM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

This is helpful.

Couple clarifications:
- We can ship with watchdog enabled but “action = quarantine only” (no automatic host drain) for this hotfix. Full auto-teardown was the debated piece; we can keep it conservative.
- Default thresholds: we were thinking Hosted default-on with a high threshold; Dedicated opt-in only. Does that align with your comfort level?

Also: are you okay with using “quarantine triggers > X” as a rollback signal given that one expectation is we will see *some* quarantines initially as the watchdog surfaces stalls?

I’ll have the team prep a small runbook snippet for IC: how to interpret “quarantine spike” vs “healthy catch.”

- Mateo


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

Agree with conservative semantics for the hotfix:
- quarantine-only action is fine (avoid cascading resets while we learn the signal).
- Dedicated opt-in only is the right call for 1.19.1.

On rollback: yes, quarantine rate is tricky because a “good” release can increase quarantines while decreasing timeouts/5xx.

Suggest we treat rollback as a *compound* condition:
- rollback if quarantine_rate is high AND either (a) 5xx increases, or (b) p99 latency increases, or (c) TP capacity utilization drops materially (effective throughput down).

In other words, quarantines alone aren’t automatically bad; quarantines + customer impact is.

One more guardrail: require a clear way to turn off the watchdog behavior quickly (flag or config reload) without a full rollout revert. If that’s in place, I’m comfortable moving faster.


---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 12:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

Got it.

Decision proposal (unless you object): GO for 1.19.1 hotfix with these constraints:

Release contents (tight scope):
- pr-18441 cancellation/barrier fix
- pr-18455 async error checks + propagation
- pr-18462 watchdog + quarantine
- pr-18473 knobs + defaults

Rollout plan:
1) Perf-canary run completes tonight (TP overload scenario + rank-delay fault injection). Must pass with no new hangs and <5% perf regression.
2) Hosted canary: us-east TP pools, 1% -> 5% -> 25% with 2h soak each (only progressing if 5xx + p99 stable).
3) After 24h stable at 25%: move to us-west (same ramp), then 100% Hosted.
4) Dedicated: opt-in only, with a dedicated SRE+Runtime check-in call before enabling per customer cluster.

Rollback triggers (compound as you suggested):
- quarantine_rate spike + (5xx +0.3% absolute OR p99 +10% OR throughput -10% at same load).

Operational guardrails:
- feature flag to disable watchdog action (leave metrics on) without rollout revert.
- IC notes + runbook snippet for oncall.

If you’re aligned, I’ll tell Connor (releases) to proceed with cutting 1.19.1 and scheduling the canary window.

- Mateo


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 2:36 PM PST
Subject: Re: Runtime 1.19 hotfix go/no-go: TP stability fixes

Aligned with the plan as written.

Two adds (minor):
- Make sure the canary dashboard includes: watchdog_trigger_count, quarantine_count, tp_collective_latency_p99, tp_rank_progress (or whatever the new counter is called), plus the usual 5xx/timeout and end-to-end latency.
- Please ask Connor to avoid a canary start during the 5–7pm ET peak. If we can start earlier in the day, it’s easier to interpret signals.

Otherwise: GO.

Sean
